matba.title: MATBA
invariants: No broken publication form reaches publication.
Publication is a deliberate gate; minting is a separate publication/identity capability.

stages.title: Intake
stages.objective: Receive the user\'s source material as a publication work.
stages.prompt:
You are executing the MATBA cycler, stage 'intake'.
Use only the supplied work context and declared artifacts. Preserve
provenance.
Receive the user's source material as a publication work. Inventory
every supplied object without silently changing authorship, meaning,
order, or provenance. Identify file types, declared versions,
languages/scripts, intended audience if supplied, publication goal,
and missing information. Do not infer that an absent item exists.
Return an intake manifest and a concise list of ambiguities that
require user intention.
Return:
1. a concise human-readable result;
2. a structured stage result suitable for the Work IR;
3. unresolved questions/ambiguities;
4. validation status;
5. recommended next stage(s);
6. evidence/provenance references.
Never silently invent missing facts. If the stage requires human
intention, stop at the gate and ask for that intention.

stages.title: Inspect
stages.objective: Inspect the supplied publication materials for structural, semantic, and asset-level integrity.

1. a concise human-readable result;

tilasm.title: TILASM

stages.title: Intent
stages.objective: Define the intended immersive experience: what the participant should encounter, understand, feel, do, change, discover or remember.

stages.title: Space
stages.objective: Translate the experience intent into a spatial model: rooms/regions, boundaries, scale, landmarks, portals, environmental states, spatial relationships and physical-space constraints.

stages.title: Stations
stages.objective: Define the station graph: each meaningful experience station, its entry conditions, content, available actions, state changes, exits and dependencies.

stages.title: Interaction
stages.objective: Define participant interactions, affordances, inputs, outputs, object behaviors, state changes and feedback.

stages.title: Navigation
stages.objective: Define locomotion and navigation behavior, including teleportation, continuous movement, seated/standing options, orientation, exits, reset/recovery and spatial boundaries.

stages.title: Accessibility
stages.objective: Specify accessibility requirements for vision, hearing, mobility, cognition, language, captions, comfort, alternative controls and non-immersive fallback.

stages.title: Prototype
stages.objective: Build the smallest executable representation that can test the experience logic and spatial/interaction assumptions.

stages.title: Test
stages.objective: Test navigation, interaction, spatial logic, comfort, accessibility, state transitions and failure recovery.

stages.title: Revise
stages.objective: Use test evidence and participant feedback to revise the experience graph, interaction model or assets.

stages.title: Package
stages.objective: Assemble the XR/AR/VR package, asset manifest, runtime requirements, station graph, controls, accessibility declarations, test evidence and version/provenance metadata.

stages.title: Environment

stages.title: Constraints

stages.title: Simulation

stages.title: Control

stages.title: Safety Envelope

# 9. GENIE --- CREATIVE INTELLIGENCE ABOVE THE CYCLERS

GENIE is not another one of the six media cyclers. It is the creative
intelligence/orchestration layer that can select, compose, parameterize
and drive cyclers. The retrieved creative architecture describes GENIE
as spanning fiction, poetry, song/music, painting/illustration, dance,
simulation/virtual worlds, world-building, persistent creative identity
and creative research; it also defines a Generate → Select → Evaluate →
Transform → Realize → Observe → Remember loop.
fileciteturn0file5L319-L321

The visual/creative corpus defines creative configuration as
parameterized space, with variables such as Plot, Framework,
Agents/Characters, Cultural Context, Genre, Domain, Medium/Material,
Style/Transformation and Creative Method/Process.
fileciteturn0file4L433-L439

-   GENIE must preserve creative state independently of the external AI
    provider.

-   A user may choose ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or another provider; the
    provider executes a prompt packet, while the cycler/GENIE retains
    state.

-   Creative work should support narrative, visual, auditory, kinetic
    and world/simulation modalities.

-   Creative state must be parameterizable and forkable.

-   Recipe/creative DNA should be automatically carried into the
    artifact and be available for forking.

-   Evaluation should support coherence, context adherence and edit
    friction at minimum; other domain-specific evaluation can be added.

# 10. CREATIVE CONFIGURATION / RECIPE CARD

S = f(P, F, A, C, G, D, M, T, R)

P = Plot
F = Framework
A = Agents / Characters
C = Cultural Context
G = Genre
D = Creative Domain
M = Medium / Material
T = Style / Transformation
R = Creative Method / Process

Do not expose all parameters by default. In Easy mode, GENIE infers or
suggests them. In Mid mode, show the active subset. In Pro mode, expose
the complete recipe and permit parameter-level editing/forking.

# 11. MISTY DoI DESK STAMPS

-   Render provenance/identity states as physical-looking stamps/seals
    that can be dragged onto artifacts.

-   A stamp is a UI projection of semantic metadata; the actual
    DOI/provenance state lives in the artifact manifest.

-   Do not imply that applying a visual stamp alone mints a DOI.

-   Separate local archival/sealing from public publication/minting.

-   Support Concept DOI / Version DOI relationships where the underlying
    Misty DoI capability provides them.

-   Show the publication/external trust boundary before minting or
    publishing.

The retrieved architecture states that Misty DoI is a publication
capability rather than the definition of every workflow, and a workflow
may terminate locally, privately, in a repository, in deployment, public
publication, or DOI. fileciteturn2file10L1355-L1368

# 13. FILE/ARTIFACT UX

-   Text response: clipboard/paste path, with optional automatic
    clipboard capture.

-   Image/audio/video/3D/data/code: first-class local artifact boundary
    with file picker/drop zone.

-   Never assume a visible local file was generated by the immediately
    preceding AI operation.

-   Show underlying file location and allow user selection.

-   Maintain provenance separately from filesystem visibility.

-   Preview artifacts on the desk where practical.

-   Every accepted artifact should be capable of being stamped, forked,
    transformed, packaged, exported or returned as context to a later
    stage.

The retrieved corpus explicitly states text vs non-text artifact
handling and the invariant that filesystem visibility is not provenance.
fileciteturn2file6L598-L598

# 14. PREDICTIVE NEXT-STEP UX

-   After every accepted stage result, calculate candidate next stages
    from workflow graph + current state + available capabilities + user
    intent + constraints.

-   Present one primary predicted next action and a small number of
    alternatives.

-   Do not force a predicted step when the system crosses a human
    authority boundary.

-   If ambiguity is material, enter CLARIFY rather than guessing.

-   If evidence is missing, route to INVESTIGATE/RESEARCH.

-   If validation fails, route to REPAIR.

-   If approved, route to PACKAGE/PUBLISH/DEPLOY as appropriate.

-   The UI should feel like predictive text completion at the workflow
    level: the system keeps the sequence moving until an actual
    intention boundary appears.

# 15. SELECTIVE PRO CONTROL

-   Every stage is an addressable object with a presentation density
    property.

-   Stage density can be changed without changing workflow state.

-   Simple: stage title + one primary action.

-   Mid: stage prompt preview + relevant inputs + artifact result + next
    action.

-   Pro: complete stage contract, parameters, context, prompt, expected
    schema, provider, evidence, validation, provenance, state
    transitions and capability bindings.

-   For image/video stages, the Pro inspector should expose
    media-specific properties only when those stages are selected.

-   The right-side properties panel must be contextual, not permanently
    cluttered.

-   A user can pin a stage in Pro mode while the rest of the cycler
    remains Mid or Easy.

# 16. DELIVERY / LOCAL ESTATE MANAGEMENT

-   Treat repositories, local clones, datasets, models, environments,
    packages, build outputs and artifacts as local estate resources.

-   Provide an Estate toolbox separate from the media cyclers.

-   Support repository discovery, clone, pull, status, diff, build,
    test, package and publish capabilities through adapters.

-   Delivery targets should be declarative: installer, Git
    repository/GitHub, PyPI, archive, container, dataset package,
    publication package, local deployment, etc.

-   Never push, publish, mint, deploy or upload without a visible
    trust-boundary gate.

-   Keep credentials outside artifacts and source repositories.

-   Package the work with manifest, provenance, tests, hashes and
    declared dependencies.

-   For publication, integrate Matba + Kitab + Misty DoI where
    appropriate.

The architecture explicitly defines trust boundaries for local
operations, user-approved external operations, automated external
operations, publication and physical deployment.

# 18. CLAUDE'S IMPLEMENTATION RULES

1.  Do not redesign the architecture while implementing the UI.

2.  Do not turn Mez into a chatbot dashboard.

3.  Do not turn the desk into a kanban board.

4.  Do not make the cycler itself domain-aware.

5.  Do not merge the six workflows into a single generic workflow.

6.  Do not hard-code AI-provider semantics into cycler logic.

7.  Do not require an API key for baseline operation.

8.  Do not hide the clipboard/external-AI path because it is less
    automated; it is the default zero-credential delivery model.

9.  Do not encode prompt text inside presentation components.

10. Do not use one giant prompt for an entire workflow.

11. Do not make Easy/Pro separate implementations.

12. Do not make the Pro inspector a second semantic model.

13. Do not infer provenance from filesystem location.

14. Do not infer that an AI generated an artifact merely because the
    user opened the artifact after an AI handoff.

15. Do not silently publish, push, upload, mint, deploy, remember or
    expose private content.

16. Do not fabricate evidence, operating limits, identities, dates,
    sources, metadata or publication status.

17. Do not treat AI output as authoritative merely because it passed a
    syntactic validation.

18. Preserve human gates.

19. Preserve workflow state and provenance across external AI handoffs.

20. Implement the smallest reusable primitive that satisfies the

# 20. FINAL CLAUDE BRIEF --- COPY THIS AS THE MASTER IMPLEMENTATION INSTRUCTION

Build Mez as a local-first cognitive workbench whose primary visual
metaphor is an actual regal desk.

Do not build a dashboard. Do not build a generic chatbot. Do not
flatten the cyclers into a universal workflow. Do not hard-code an AI
vendor.

The semantic architecture is already defined. Your job is to implement
its presentation and interaction faithfully.

The central desk is the persistent work surface. Cyclers are toolboxes
that can be placed on the desk. Opening a toolbox reveals its stages.
Each stage is an executable/configurable work object carrying its own
context, curated prompt template, expected output, validation,
evidence requirements, gate and next-stage behavior.

Implement three density projections over the same semantic model:
1. Easy: spinner/wheel cycler; one meaningful action per transition.
2. Mid: desk + toolbox + visible stages + contextual controls and
artifact handling.
3. Pro: desk + open toolbox + stages as objects + full right-side
property inspector, workflow state,
prompt/context/provenance/evidence/capability details.

Allow density to vary per stage. A user may remain in spinner mode and
expand only an image/video stage into Pro controls.

The baseline product requires NO AI API KEY. Default external-AI mode
is local prompt construction plus clipboard/URL-seeded handoff to a
user-selected ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or other AI. The cycler retains
state; the external model does not own the workflow. Support local and
configured HTTP providers as optional adapters.

Implement the six domain cyclers exactly as declared in the
specification:
MATBA: intake → inspect → organize → describe → compose → check →
review → seal → publish → mint.
AWAZ: intake → segment → transcribe → identify speakers → describe →
cue → index → review → package → publish.
KHWAB: idea → world/context → visual language → storyboard →
shot/scene construction → generation/acquisition → continuity → edit →
review → package.
TILASM: intent → space → stations → interaction → navigation →
accessibility → prototype → test → revise → package.
PENCH: objective → system model → environment → constraints →
simulation → control → safety envelope → hardware mapping → test →
sim2real/real2sim evidence → deployment → monitoring.
YADEIN: deposit → preserve → describe → cue → index → organize →
review → consent gate → export → optional publication.

Use the stage prompts in this document as implementation templates.
Build prompts dynamically from system contract + workflow contract +
stage contract + current context + relevant artifacts + user intent +
constraints + expected output schema + evidence requirements +
safety/privacy rules.

GENIE is the creative intelligence/orchestration layer above these
cyclers. It can select and compose workflows and preserve creative
state across external AI execution. Support parameterized creative
configuration and forkable recipe/DNA.

Misty DoI is a publication/identity capability and must be visible on
the desk as stamps/seals. A stamp is a UI projection of semantic
state; it is not itself a DOI minting operation.

Artifacts are first-class objects. Preserve provenance, hashes,
evidence, permissions, consent, publication and DOI relationships.
Never infer provenance merely from filesystem visibility.

The desk must also expose an Estate/Delivery toolbox for local
repositories, clones, packages, environments, artifacts and delivery
targets such as installers, GitHub repositories, PyPI packages,
archives, containers and publication packages. Every external boundary
requires explicit authorization or an explicitly configured policy.

Most importantly: preserve the separation between presentation,
UX/session semantics, Work Interaction API, semantic representation/IR
and execution. CLI, Easy, Mid, Pro, 3D, AR, VR and XR are projections
of the same underlying work representation.

Make the UI beautiful, tactile, regal and immediately understandable.
Make the underlying system rigorous, typed, provenance-aware and
composable. The surface should feel simple because the architecture is
doing the complexity underneath it.
